Answer: D
Reason: The combination of right-sided findings (pleural effusion, atelectasis/hypoplasia) and a prominent left second arc (suggesting an enlarged pulmonary artery or atrium due to volume overload) is characteristic of Scimitar syndrome, which involves partial anomalous pulmonary venous return (PAPVR) from the right lung to the systemic venous circulation.
